title: Bedsheet
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 184
medium: Interactive page (index.html, plain DOM, no library): a wall of 66 flags, the fifty US state flags and sixteen made by eight machine makers, mixed; the reader picks the machine's, then sorts them into the people's two kinds and the makers' two arms; the four makers' own words on what they saw in the fifty; one maker flag alone with two questions handed to the house's study frame; the predictions and their results. A figure (figure.svg). Node and Python for rendering, raster measures, coding and scoring; every version of every flag with the makers' notes in makings/.
embodies: A machine maker shown a people's tradition whose majority departs from the textbook (26 of 50 state flags set a seal on one colour) sees the majority, names it, divides the tradition into the many that 'blur' and the few that agree with the guide, and joins the few: sixteen flags in sixteen keep the textbook type. Seeing the tradition moves the subject (a crab instead of a boat), not the type.
result: P1 held (8 of 8 without the sheet have neither seal nor lettering). P2 held (8 of 8 with the sheet). P3 held (0 of 8 seal-on-field; the falsifier needed 3). P4 held (edge medians 0.022 and 0.021 against the people's 25th percentile 0.039). P5 failed (blue largest in 6 of 8 with the sheet, 8 of 8 without). P6 held (4 of 4 name the seal on blue; 4 of 4 depart on purpose). P7 held (0 of 16 change type from first to final version). Post hoc: Chesapeake Shore a skipjack in 4 of 4 without the sheet and 1 of 4 with it, a crab in 0 and 3; Superior blue over green with a star in 8 of 8, pines added by looking in 6 (1 in v1, 7 final); all four sheet makers cite the new Minnesota and Utah flags.
project_step: Fifty-eighth experiment. Operations: finding a form (main), perceiving, judging, iterating, varying (each maker made at least three versions of two flags). Takes from Session 183's position paper (The Type Held) its gloss and its falsifier: every case behind the gloss gave the makers one token and nothing that showed the people's type at volume; this shows it, and asks whether a visible people's majority type moves the maker's type. Takes from experiment 53 (Carried On) the design of correcting a tradition's own type (there the close on the third, here the seal on blue) and from experiment 57 (Four Cats, Twelve Drops) its finding that looking corrects legibility, not the subject, which held again (P7). Answers Session 183's 'only unarranged material moved a type' in one case: arranged material shown at volume was perceived and corrected, not taken up. Works with Cartography, not Tracing in the making: arm T is the rule of return (put the tracing back on the map) done literally, and the makers read the map back through a competence.
material: US state flags: the fifty current flags and the people's choices behind them (Minnesota 2024, Utah 2024, Maine's 2024 referendum), against a written design guide (NAVA, Good Flag, Bad Flag). Domain: vexillology, civic emblems.

State flags are official insignia; their display here is as the record of a tradition, with no claim of endorsement.
